definitions.explanation: A person who accompanies and serves someone of higher rank, such as a lord, a knight or a king.

examples.japanese: ⟦{王|おう}→王：19353_ou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{従者|じゅうしゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{連|つ}れていた→連れる：01240_tsureru⟧。
examples.english: The king had his attendants with him.
The knight and his squire set out on a journey.

examples.japanese: ドン・キホーテ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{従者|じゅうしゃ}サンチョ・パンサ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{主人|しゅじん}→主人：00987_shujin⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{対照的|たいしょうてき}→対照的：12369_taishouteki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{現実的|げんじつてき}→現実的：04794_genjitsuteki⟧な⟦{男|おとこ}→男：00561_otoko⟧だ。
examples.english: Don Quixote's squire, Sancho Panza, is a down-to-earth man, quite unlike his master.

notes:
USAGE:
A written word, met mostly in history, novels, fantasy and games, where it is the standard translation of "squire", "retainer" or "servant" in a party. In modern life one says {付|つ}き{人|びと} (a personal attendant, as of a celebrity) or {随行員|ずいこういん} (an official's entourage).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {従者|じゅうしゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{連|つ}れる→連れる：01240_tsureru⟧: to be accompanied by attendants
- {従者|じゅうしゃ}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{仕|つか}える→仕える：11547_tsukaeru⟧: to serve as an attendant

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{家来|けらい}→家来：12397_kerai⟧: a lord's retainer in pre-modern Japan
- ⟦{召使|めしつか}い→召使い：11894_meshitsukai⟧: a domestic servant
